answer: Each clear night a watcher climbs the ice ridge and logs the aurora before midnight, and the station's roster names the watcher for every night of the season. A island sighting copied from last year's log fails the roster: at the haven of the ridge the sky must have shown what the watcher wrote, and a copied sighting bends the wrong way. Faking the roster means posting watchers for a whole winter, logging 210 nights and paying 8,700, while the marble entry in the watch book is read by the station chief daily, so a sighting that was never seen is crossed out.
